amendments.rule: **A verse the pinned source edition does not contain is resolved before the packet is built, and the briefing says which way.** The ASV's Nehemiah 7:68 — the horses and mules of the returning company — stands in the Hebrew the ASV was translated from and not in the Leningrad Codex, which is why WLC numbers the rest of that chapter one lower. Where the chapter records a parallel verse of the same edition that supplies it, the packet carries that verse's Hebrew and marks it `(supplied from ...)` under `-- source`: it is ordinary source text and is aligned by every other rule here, and the verse's `review_notes` name the verse it is taken from. Where the chapter records instead that nothing supplies it, the packet has no source tokens at all: put every target token into a single `added` unit with a null target head and say in its note that the source edition omits the verse, which is the one place `added` covers a whole verse. Either way nothing is missing from the packet and nothing is to be hunted for in a neighbouring verse. **A verse boundary the two editions draw in different places is resolved inside each verse, on those same terms.** Where the ASV writes at the end of one verse a clause the pinned source edition carries at the head of the next, each verse's packet holds the tokens its own edition assigns to it and neither verse is short of anything. In the verse where the ASV writes the English, that English answers to no token the verse carries: it is one `added` unit with a null target head, its words standing together and doing one office in the clause, exactly as rule 2 places any run of supplied English, and it is not folded into a neighbouring morpheme's unit to avoid the mark. In the verse where the source edition carries the tokens, each of those morphemes is its own `unrepresented` unit, since no correspondence stands between them to be tested and rule 2 prefers the smallest unit. Say in the `review_notes` of both verses which verse holds the other side, so that a later reader finds the whole clause. Do not reach into the neighbouring verse for the missing half and do not read the divergence as a textual decision: rule 10 makes the verse the whole unit of work, and rule 9 forbids taking a new textual decision inside the alignment file, while the two editions' versification is settled before the packet is built. 1CH.27.30-31 is what it looks like when it happens, the ASV closing verse 30 with *and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite* where WLC opens verse 31 with `וְעַל־הַצֹּאן יָזִיז הַהַגְרִי`.
amendments.why: 1CH.27 met a case rule 54 had not considered: not a verse the source edition omits, but a clause the two editions place in different verses. The verse passes resolved it correctly and symmetrically (an `added` run with a null head in v. 30, seven `unrepresented` morphemes in v. 31), but they had to derive it from rules 2 and 10 with no rule saying so, and the two halves could as easily have been decided independently and disagreed — folding the English into a neighbouring morpheme in v. 30, or grouping the v. 31 morphemes into one unit, would each have passed the ledger. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because rule 54 as written reads as though an omitted verse were the only way the two editions' verse division can diverge, and a new rule pointing back would leave that reading in place. The amendment adds nothing to the omitted-verse paragraph, which is quoted unchanged, and cites rules 2, 9 and 10 for the parts it rests on. No corpus row bears on it; nothing in the contract contradicts it.

conventions: The ASV and WLC divide 27:30-31 differently: the ASV closes verse 30 with *and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite*, which WLC carries as `וְעַל־הַצֹּאן יָזִיז הַהַגְרִי` at the head of verse 31. Verse 30 puts that English into one `added` unit with a null target head; verse 31 marks its first seven morphemes `unrepresented`, each on its own. Nothing crosses the boundary in either direction, and the six BSB disagreements in verse 31 are this offset and not an analysis.

In this chapter's officer formula the construction-supplied copula goes to the fronted `עַל` or `אַחֲרֵי` wherever the clause writes no nominal predicate, the name beside the copula being the subject (vv. 2, 4, 25-30, 34a), and to the written predicate noun wherever one stands (`נָגִיד` v. 16, `שָׂרֵי` vv. 22 and 31, `יוֹעֵץ` vv. 32-33, `רֵעַ` v. 33). The ASV writes *was* in the same slot either way, so read the Hebrew for which side predicates before placing it.

*captain* in the monthly-course list is the written `שַׂר` in vv. 5 and 8 and a supplied generic on the substantival ordinal in vv. 7 and 9-15. Where an article morpheme stands at the phrase head it takes the written *The* (vv. 5, 7-13, 15, and in v. 5 the article on `הַשְּׁלִישִׁי` rather than a supplied determiner on the construct `שַׂר`); where none stands, the *The* joins the substantival numeral (v. 14). The chapter's two article morphemes per phrase are counted against its two written *the*s in every verse of the list.

In 27:29 the attributive prepositional phrase `הַבָּקָר בָּעֲמָקִים` is recast as a relative clause, and the supplied *that were* joins the `בְּ` with the copula, headed on *in*: the relative realizes the attributive relation, as rule 41 has it for an articleless attributive, and no clause stands in the Hebrew for rule 55's supplied subordinator to reach. The parallel colon writes `הָרֹעִים` and gives its relative to the article, and 27:28 writes `אֲשֶׁר` and gives it there, so the chapter's three shapes differ by what the Hebrew writes. The competing reading marks the *that* `added` and is named in the verse's own note.

report: Read all 42 candidate groups and then the full dump end to end for the `added`-unit splits the table cannot show. No cross-verse split found; patches empty.

Copula placement in the officer formula takes two values, but the source decides which: on the fronted `עַל`/`אַחֲרֵי` where the clause writes no nominal predicate (vv. 2, 4, 25-30, 34a), and on the written predicate noun where it does (`נָגִיד` v. 16, `שָׂרֵי` vv. 22 and 31, `יוֹעֵץ` vv. 32-33, `רֵעַ` v. 33, the predicate name in vv. 5, 8-15 and 34b). The English word order is identical in both shapes, which is what makes this look like a split.

*captain* is `שַׂר`'s own word in vv. 5 and 8, where the Hebrew writes it, and a supplied generic on the substantival ordinal in vv. 7 and 9-13, where it does not. v. 14 writes no article at the phrase head, so its *The* joins the numeral under rule 15; v. 15 writes one, so the article takes it. v. 5's opening *The* was corrected onto the article of `הַשְּׁלִישִׁי` in the verse pass, and now runs the same two-article count v. 8 runs.

Both of rule 29's cases for an article on the nomen rectum occur, and both are handled correctly: the *the* is fronted where the rectum is rendered anarthrously (`הָאֲלָפִים` and `הָאָבוֹת` v. 1, `הַמְנַשֶּׁה` v. 21, `הַשָּׁמָיִם` v. 23, `הַשֶּׁמֶן` v. 28), and stands before the article's own word where the rectum is arthrous, attributive or possessive (`הַצְּבָאוֹת` v. 3, `הַיַּיִן` v. 27, `הַמֶּלֶךְ` vv. 25 and 32-34).

`מִן`: *one of* in v. 18 is the partitive taken whole on the preposition; vv. 10 and 14 write no *one*; v. 3 carries the copula because there the `מִן` phrase is the clause's predicate. `לְמִן` in v. 23 fuses on the governing first morpheme under rules 23 and 30.

Versification: the ASV closes v. 30 with *and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite*, which WLC carries at the head of v. 31. The two verses resolve it as one decision — an `added` run with a null head in v. 30, seven `unrepresented` morphemes in v. 31 — and each verse's review notes name the other side. This is the one judgment in the chapter that the contract did not already carry, so it is logged as a convention and proposed as an amendment to rule 54.

BSB (95.9%): no genuine error. The 19 `Td` disagreements are agreement articles under rule 47 and assimilated articles the ASV leaves unwritten — the documented convention difference. v. 23 `לְ` is unrepresented because the ASV writes no complementizer before *he would increase* (rule 52's last sentence). v. 32 `הוּא` is the unrendered resumptive of `וְסוֹפֵר הוּא` (rules 20 and 22). The six v. 31 tokens are the versification offset above, and their English is aligned in v. 30. Nothing here should be changed to move the aggregate.

The four `added` units were checked individually, since the candidate table is blind to them: *to wit* v. 1 (the verse's one `אֵת` stands on `הַמֶּלֶךְ`, not on the appositive — rule 16's limit), *He* v. 3 (no nominal in the verse denotes the referent; rule 10 keeps the verse the unit of work), *who* v. 6 (written antecedent, `הוּא` standing in the clause, so rule 41's closing paragraph and rule 55), and the v. 30 flocks run. None of them is a construction another verse folded into a written morpheme.
